name: Path Interception by PATH Environment Variable

sigma_rules.title: Trusted Path Bypass via Windows Directory Spoofing
sigma_rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)

strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Hijack Execution Flow using Path Interception by PATH Environment Variable.

analytics.name: Analytic 0009
analytics.guidance: Abnormal modification of the PATH environment variable or registry keys controlling system paths, combined with execution of binaries named after legitimate system tools from user-writable directories. Defender correlates registry modifications, file creation of suspicious binaries, and process execution paths inconsistent with baseline system directories.

tuning.description: PATH environment keys under HKCU and HKLM to monitor for changes.
List of high-value system binaries commonly hijacked (e.g., net.exe, python.exe, powershell.exe).
Correlation window between PATH modification and execution of a hijacked binary.

analytics.name: Analytic 0010
analytics.guidance: User modification of the $PATH environment variable in shell configuration files or direct runtime PATH changes, followed by execution of binaries from user-controlled directories. Defender observes file edits to ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, or /etc/paths.d and process execution resolving to unexpected binary locations.

tuning.description: Set of shell startup files where PATH changes should be flagged.
Directories (e.g., /usr/local/bin) considered safe to avoid FP.

log_sources.name: linux:osquery
log_sources.channel: Execution of binary resolved from $PATH not located in /usr/bin or /bin

analytics.name: Analytic 0011
analytics.guidance: Modification of PATH or HOME environment variables through shell config files, launchctl, or /etc/paths.d entries, combined with process execution from attacker-controlled directories. Defender correlates file changes in /etc/paths.d with process execution resolving to malicious binaries.

tuning.description: Baseline applications expected in user PATH directories.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: File modification in /etc/paths.d or user shell rc files

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Process execution path inconsistent with baseline PATH directories
